data.narrative:
Oxa is a Series D-stage autonomous systems company in the Drones & Autonomous sector, having raised $103M to date. The comparable universe includes six private peers in the same sector (Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, Elroy Air, and one additional firm), with no public comparables available for direct benchmarking.

Given the lack of sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage peers with disclosed valuation data, the peer-median approach is not applicable. Instead, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 1.5x step-up multiplier typical of Series D advancement to the $103M total capital raised proxy. This method yields an implied valuation of $154M. The analysis produces a triangulated range of $131M (low), $154M (median), and $178M (high), bracketing the stage-progression result with ±15% sensitivity bounds.

The primary uncertainty stems from the limited precision of comparable data in this subsector; no same-stage private peer set exists with sufficient disclosure to validate multiples on revenue, gross margin, or customer concentration. The $154M midpoint estimate should be treated as directional pending (1) access to peer-level financial metrics or (2) evidence of material customer traction or contractual backlog not reflected in the raised capital proxy. Investors should stress-test this range against unit economics and burn rate relative to the $103M deployed.
